target.title: feat: support GCP broker metadata auth
target.body:
## Summary

- Adds explicit `CRABBOX_GCP_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=metadata` support for brokered GCP coordinators running with an attached Google Cloud service identity.
- Preserves service-account-key auth as the default and fails closed for partial key pairs, invalid source names, or keyless config without explicit metadata opt-in.
- Rejects metadata redirects and responses without Google's `Metadata-Flavor: Google` marker before trusting a token.
- Retries connection/startup failures plus transient `429`, `499`, and all `5xx` responses with exponential backoff, a five-second attempt timeout covering headers and body, and a one-minute overall deadline.
- Refreshes tokens before Google's five-minute metadata cache boundary and preserves the HTTP status for non-JSON errors.
- Updates readiness diagnostics, environment typing, provider docs, and regression coverage without retaining a contributor-branch changelog edit.

Refs https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/1016.

## Config and secret implications

Google-hosted coordinators can set `CRABBOX_GCP_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=metadata` plus `GCP_PROJECT_ID` or `CRABBOX_GCP_PROJECT`. Portable coordinators continue to use both `GCP_CLIENT_EMAIL` and `GCP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Metadata mode sends no Crabbox credential to the metadata endpoint; it makes the documented fixed-host request with `Metadata-Flavor: Google` and uses the returned short-lived access token only for Google Compute API calls.

## Verification

Integration head: `0df05f2b36636866fcc52ec6386f41eb2a3630d4`

- `go test -race ./...`
- `npm test --prefix worker` — 930 passed, 3 skipped
- `npm test --prefix worker -- --run test/gcp.test.ts test/fleet.test.ts` — 464 passed
- `npm run format:check --prefix worker`
- `npm run lint --prefix worker`
- `npm run check --prefix worker`
- `npm run check:node --prefix worker`
- `npm run build --prefix worker`
- `npm run build:node --prefix worker`
- `./scripts/check-docs.sh` — 54 command docs, 73 providers, 213 Markdown files, docs site built
- AutoReview local repair loop — one accepted stalled-body timeout finding fixed; second pass clean
- AutoReview against integration base `e5b1f2f546915ac80d102ba5884851d708c3cd55` — clean, no accepted or actionable findings
- Exact-head hosted CI — all 12 checks passed: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29057994423), [connector smokes](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29057994426)
- Endpoint, response-marker, token-cache, access-scope, and retry contracts checked against current official Compute Engine documentation

## Live proof

Provider-code candidate `19268d546ded74d904e4eee1e43e366ba5625c77` passed on a real GCP `e2-standard-2` lease. The branch's bundled `GCPClient` ran with only `CRABBOX_GCP_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=metadata` and the metadata-derived project ID, acquired the attached service-account token, and completed the real aggregated Compute instance-list request:

```text
metadata_token_acquisition=ok compute_api_request=ok crabbox_machine_count=0
```

At exact head `0df05f2b36636866fcc52ec6386f41eb2a3630d4`, a fresh real `e2-standard-2` lease verified the SHA-256 of `worker/src/gcp.ts` and the live test before execution. With the project default service account attached, the exact code acquired a real metadata token and reached the Compute API; the request then failed closed at `compute.firewalls.get` because that account lacks Compute IAM. The first diagnostic also proved that broker-created VMs have zero attached service accounts unless one is requested explicitly.

Every diagnostic and canary lease was deleted, and `go run ./cmd/crabbox list --provider gcp --json` returned `null` after each attempt. No static GCP key was copied into a lease and no token was printed or persisted.

The remaining exact-head live gate is an attached service account with the documented Compute IAM permissions. Do not merge until that privileged lifecycle is rerun or a maintainer explicitly accepts the earlier full Compute proof plus the exact-head token-acquisition proof.
